svg.title: Index Types
svg.desc: Index Types. Beyond B-trees: hash, GIN for arrays, JSON and text, GiST, BRIN for time-ordered data, and partial and expression indexes. Step 1, One B-tree for everything: One B-tree per column: 3,464 kB for 3,000 open orders, lower(email) missed, @> scans all products. Step 2, Partial and expression: A partial index holds only the 3,000 open orders (88 kB); an index on lower(email) serves the login. Step 3, BRIN and GIN: BRIN keeps a min and max per 128 pages (24 kB, correlation 1.00); GIN maps each key to its rows. Step 4, Costs and limits: A reworded WHERE skips the partial index, hash handles = only, BRIN needs order, GIN queues writes.

g.text: One B-tree per column: 3,464 kB for 3,000 open orders, lower(email) missed, @> scans all products.
A partial index holds only the 3,000 open orders (88 kB); an index on lower(email) serves the login.
BRIN keeps a min and max per 128 pages (24 kB, correlation 1.00); GIN maps each key to its rows.
A reworded WHERE skips the partial index, hash handles = only, BRIN needs order, GIN queues writes.
orders_open_idx · partial B-tree on created_at · 11 pages
Limit 20: no sort, one leaf page
keys are email as stored: customer42@example.com
lower(email) is another expression → not used
unused: the query asks for lower(email)
a plain Seq Scan took 26 ms
keys are whole documents in jsonb order
@> looks inside a document → not used
Acme Shop sample data on PostgreSQL 18.6 · plans from EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS), one run on a laptop, timings rounded
Also: GiST for overlapping ranges and the nearest point · SP-GiST for quad-trees and IP prefixes · MySQL InnoDB: no partial or BRIN indexes
